doc.title: Stefon Harris interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 11, 2020

title: Reflection on the United States and empathy
summary: Asked about the state of the country, Harris says the root problem is lack of empathy and praises president-elect Biden's use of the word.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Politics, race and the state of the country

blocks.x: I wish I could remember which musician said, “Yeah jazz is a great field, you can become a hundredaire.” So I’m going to ask you probably a tough question, then we’ll see if we have any questions from other people who are viewing. Do you have anything that you’d like to reflect on and say about the current situation the United States is in?

I look back, prior to our current administration, and I think what’s at the center of what brought us to this situation is a lack of empathy. I’m going to always go back to empathy. And I should preface it by saying that I don’t think that empathy has morality. Empathy is not good or bad, empathy has been used for evil throughout history, and it’s been used for good. The most important thing though is to be able to quiet the ego first and to listen and to understand the environment in which your ideas exist. And I think what was occurring in our country was that we weren’t listening to each other. You know people on the left, people in the middle, were totally shocked by one another. We’re not paying attention to who we are and we’re not getting to the root of what we really care about because we’re focused on this right or wrong, this projection of right or wrong is an egocentric perspective. So for me if there’s anything I hope to contribute to this world is I want to amplify the value, the understanding of the value of empathy, getting people to say, I always like to say when I’m teaching about empathy is that it doesn’t matter what you think. It’s just irrelevant. Right? Right now you should be just trying to understand

the person in front of you. No judgement at all. Then once it’s there then you can have some sense of judgement in whichever way you choose. And then it’s up to your moral code. It’s about how you will behave. But I don’t think we’re in a situation right now where we have been paying attention to one another. And it’s been great, honestly, to see president-elect Biden use the word empathy as much as he does because I think that’s what’s going to need to happen to get the gears of our Congress working properly.
Well thank you for sharing that. So Michelle do we have any folks who would like to ask something of Mr. Harris?
